item.location: approach.tex cor:dense; appendix app:dense and app:models power neuron
item.statement: 2B_p p/(p-1) = sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1)) is exactly Morwani's max L_{2,3} margin; their network attains the bound so C_3 = 2B_p
item.what_to_check: Verify constant in Morwani's modular-addition theorem

chk.evidence:
I fetched https://arxiv.org/html/2311.07568 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07568. The paper is "Feature emergence via margin maximization: case studies in algebraic tasks" by Morwani, Edelman, Oncescu, Zhao and Kakade; the arXiv comment says "Spotlight at ICLR 2024".

What the paper says: Theorem 7 (cyclic groups) covers a prime p>2, width m >= 4(p-1), quadratic activations, and the neuron phi({u,v,w},a,b)=(u_a+v_b)^2 w. It states: "the maximum L_{2,3}-margin is gamma* = sqrt(2/27)*1/(p^{1/2}(p-1))". At the maximum, each neuron is a single-frequency cosine and every frequency zeta in {1..(p-1)/2} is used by some neuron.

How it matches our paper:
- Our power neuron at n=2 is exactly their neuron.
- b=nu=3 is their L_{2,3} norm.
- Our margin definitions g, h and gamma*_b match theirs.

Arithmetic: 2B_p p/(p-1) = 4(6p)^{-3/2} p/(p-1) = (2/(3 sqrt6))/(p^{1/2}(p-1)) = sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1)). I checked this numerically at p=3, 5 and 113; the two sides agree to machine precision.

Attainment: their theorem gives the global maximum, and their construction attains it. Our bound is an upper bound at every width. Since the two are equal, C_3 = 2B_p follows. One caveat is that their theorem assumes width m >= 4(p-1).

The intro sentence ("every frequency is used, one frequency per neuron") also matches Theorem 7.

recommended_citations.why: Theorem 7 gives the maximum L_{2,3} margin sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1)) for quadratic networks (u_a+v_b)^2 w of width >= 4(p-1) on modular addition. It supports cor:dense, app:dense and the claim C_3 = 2B_p. The existing bib entry is correct.
